items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: "Big Boy" had been in the Chikito in an orchestra lead by Glen Pacque who had managed to make his home in Switzerland near the beginning of the second world war."

ctx.x: Felix Debrit who had asked me in Paris when I met him during the festival about leading an orchestra in the Chikito came to see me in Geneva, with Johnny Simmen. Johnny came along to help Felix persuade me into taking a group into the Chikito and they succeeded. I accepted the offer. Not because I wanted to be a leader. I never felt as though I had the qualifications to be one, but I decided to give it a try.

Felix told me that he was in contact with Ernest "Bass" Hill and Norman Lester, a pianist, both of whom I knew. "Bass" and I had been in a Benny Carter orchestra together, also in the Philippines. Norman I had known for years, but we had never worked together. Felix was also in touch with an American tenor sax man named Fred Palmer, who was in Italy. I didn't know this fellow, but was told that he had been a member of Noble Sissle's orchestra at one time. That was no worhty recommendation to me, but it was Felix…

After I had finished at the Grillzon dancing with Jack Dieval, we did a radio show in Lausanne, and I was invited to spend a few days with Johnny Simmen, whose real name is Hans George Simmen, and his wife Lisette, who dosen't like her real name, which is Liza. I had met them, Johnny's sister, her husband and a girl named Bettina Blockinger, the first time I did a concert in Zurich with BonByas and the Edouard's band.
